title: Null Run environment kits: Drowned Records, Switchyard Chapel, After Hours Pavilion

seam_behavior.walls: All eight wall tiles are RGB 128x128 and seamless on both axes. Opposite edge rows and columns are exactly equal. Tiles 07 and 08 are landmark accent panels: each wraps independently, and the pair is an authored adjacent motif rather than a continuous split image.
seam_behavior.flats: All four flats are RGB 64x64 and seamless on both axes. Opposite edge rows and columns are exactly equal.
seam_behavior.props: All props are RGBA 96x128 cut-outs with at least three transparent pixels on every edge and feet/bases at the bottom. They are not tiled and have no opaque rectangular backdrop.

selection.notes: Suggestions only. Codex owns seeded selection and native integration. Use one kit as a whole-run or whole-tier identity; do not mix kits per room. Keep walls 07 and 08 together.
selection.suggested_seed_use: Derive the set from the run seed as a separate choice from map layout, so the same layout can be replayed with a different kit.

floor_variation.notes: Metadata only; Codex implements any variation. Flats 01-04 are a complete floor/ceiling set and should not be mixed with another kit.
rules: flats/02 is the utility or service floor for plant rooms, trenches and back-of-house.
flats/04 is the lit or fixture ceiling; it is never a floor.
Vary floors by room function, not by random per-tile substitution.

sets.name: DROWNED RECORDS
sets.description: A flood-marked paper archive and pump bureaucracy: chalk-bone filing walls, petrol waterlines, silted ceramic panels and copper shelf trim. Filing drawers, tide gauges, pressure seals and layered paper strata surround a circular flood register bolted through a filing facade. Old water is suggested by stains, not live physics.

landmark.name: The Flood Register
landmark.description: A circular tide-register wheel embedded in a wall of filing drawers. Its copper ring is bolted through the cabinet face; the scale carries two zero marks and the pointer sweeps into a drawer bank. The paired panels are a filing facade (07) and the register plate (08).

service_lamp.description: A caged copper inspection lantern on a paper-wrapped plinth with a small silt gauge. Small freestanding floor fixture.

cable_shrine.description: A pallet of compressed paper bales under ceramic pressure seals, copper straps, a hand lever and a blank record plate. Freestanding archive utility object.

directory_sign.description: A two-legged lectern carrying the portable tide register wheel, a hanging blank slip and a stack of ledgers. Landmark directory object with a solid base.

sets.gameplay_notes: Cosmetic material set only; no mechanics, collision, light or sound changes are claimed. Mid-dark petrol, slate and copper surfaces keep bright binding-ring colours legible. Suggested as a whole-run or whole-tier identity, never mixed per room.

sets.name: SWITCHYARD CHAPEL
sets.description: An ossified power exchange and ceramic relay forest: ivory porcelain brick, rust-red iron, charcoal cable braids and warm amber indicators. Chunky fluting, stacked relay niches and sagging bundled cable give clear silhouettes around a silent radial conductor fan. No religious symbol is copied from an existing game.

landmark.name: The Silent Conductor
landmark.description: A nine-fin porcelain insulator fan around a dead charcoal hub. Two cable braids descend from the hub; one terminates in a blank porcelain cap. The paired panels are the fan (07) and a braided cable gallery (08). No live power, bloom or motion is depicted.

service_lamp.description: A squat porcelain petticoat pedestal carrying a caged amber pilot lamp under a rust hood. Small static fixture.

cable_shrine.description: A freestanding iron rack of three ceramic relay spools wrapped by sagging cable braids, with one amber pilot. Utility sculpture, not an altar or a passage.

directory_sign.description: A two-legged iron annunciator board with twelve amber relay windows, twin porcelain horns, conduit and a blank nameplate. Directory object; no text is drawn.

sets.gameplay_notes: Cosmetic material set only; no electrical, combat or traversal mechanics are claimed. Rust-red and charcoal fields are broken by ivory porcelain and small amber indicators, leaving bright binding rings distinct. Suggested as a whole-run or whole-tier identity.

sets.name: AFTER HOURS PAVILION
sets.description: A deserted transit and convention concourse: dusty plum plaster, worn brass, pale geometric terrazzo and shuttered service windows. Deeply folded baffles, unclaimed queue apparatus and deliberately contradictory abstract pictogram wayfinding lead to an impossible split-faced ticket and directory kiosk.

landmark.name: The Split-Faced Night Kiosk
landmark.description: A two-panel kiosk facade. Panel 07 is a real directory face with a route map, blank slot columns and a ticket recess. Panel 08 is the same architecture inlaid solid in terrazzo with no opening; its route line leaves the map and re-enters at the wrong height.

service_lamp.description: A terrazzo-based brass bollard with a folded plum shade, a cream underside and a call button plate. Small static fixture.

cable_shrine.description: A single brass stanchion with a heavy base, a retractable belt sagging in a loose decorative loop, and a blank split-arrow tag. Freestanding queue hardware.

directory_sign.description: A two-legged kiosk whose left face has a working directory and ticket slot while its right face is the same architecture inlaid solid in terrazzo, including a pale inlaid ticket stub. No door or opening is drawn.

sets.gameplay_notes: Cosmetic material set only; no transit, queue or door mechanics are claimed. Plum and slate fields with pale terrazzo and brass keep bright binding-ring colours readable. Suggested as a whole-run or whole-tier identity; the split-faced kiosk is a deliberate impossible detail, not a hidden route.
